content:
arya: quick heads-up — I repro'd a ~12% E2E regression on 8k-context bf16 runs after the recent kernel-selector change (prefers fused->flash-hybrid). seen on A100s in dedicated pool :eyes:
arya: benchmark command I used:
```
./bench_runner --model llama-13b --seq_len 8192 --dtype bf16 --batch 1 --selector new-kernel-policy --repeat 50
```
arya: nvprof/flame graph shows a few layers falling back to paged-attn with large stride copies, and a measurable copy/pad in KV build step. attaching short snippet:
```
Layer 10: chosen=paged_attention_paged_kv  latency=3.6ms
Layer 11: chosen=flash_hybrid_fused    latency=1.4ms
KV build copy: 0.9ms (padding 128 bytes per row)
```
mike: can you paste the kernel-selection log (selector debug) + perf-bot output? wondering if thresholding logic mis-ranked kernels for bf16 stride patterns
arya: perf-bot output pasted below:
```
perf-bot: selector_decision: layer_range=0-7 -> flash_hybrid_fused
perf-bot: selector_decision: layer_range=8-22 -> paged_attention_paged_kv (estimated_throughput_drop=18%)
perf-bot: kv_layout=interleaved dtype=bf16 stride=40 bytes align=16
```
sophia: hmm looks like interleaved KV + bf16 causes odd padding on our paged-backed allocator. when stride % warp_size != 0 we insert a small copy to align pages which kills latency. try REDWOOD_KV_LAYOUT=separate to avoid per-row interleave copies
devon: ran a quick A/B on a canary A100:
```
baseline (interleaved + new-selector): 100 tokens/s
separate-layout + new-selector: 110 tokens/s
old-selector + interleaved: 112 tokens/s
```
devon: separate layout recovered ~10%, still ~2% behind old-selector. suggests kernel ranking still slightly off for tail layers
mike: thx. plan: tweak selector to prefer flash_hybrid for layers where kv_stride%alignment != 0 or estimated_copy_cost > threshold. I'll open a small patch to add the rule and a perf guardrail. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321
infra-bot: CI note: please add an 8k-bf16 smoke to the selector e2e suite (covers paged vs fused choices).
arya: will add the smoke test + a short repro script in infra/tests/bench_8k_bf16.sh. assigning to me.
sophia: +1. also add a unit that simulates odd strides so we don't regress on padding again.
mike: after PR lands let's run a dedicated canary on one reserved pool tomorrow and watch token/s and tail-latency percentiles.
arya: sounds good — I'll open follow-ups and tag @sophia for allocator notes. thanks all :thumbsup:
